hook: Denis Yarats pursued a PhD in artificial intelligence at New York University, focusing on reinforcement learning, and collaborated with Facebook AI Research on projects including end-to-end learning for negotiation dialogues. His research produced DrQ and DrQ-v2, data-augmented reinforcement learning algorithms for training vision-based agents efficiently, and Proto-RL, a self-supervised method using prototypical representations. In August 2022 he co-founded Perplexity AI with Aravind Srinivas, Johnny Ho, and Andy Konwinski, taking on the role of Chief Technology Officer. As CTO, he has helped build the technical infrastructure behind Perplexity's search-grounded answer engine, which launched publicly in December 2022.

reading.body:
Denis Yarats moved from reinforcement learning research to building search infrastructure at Perplexity AI, shifting from improving sample efficiency to scaling inference over real-time web data.

His PhD work on DrQ and DrQ-v2 focused on a narrow, acute problem: making vision-based agents learn from fewer training examples. This work was foundational but bounded. As CTO at Perplexity, launched publicly in December 2022, he now builds systems that must handle scale in a different direction: serving many users querying live web content and generating cited answers in real time. Both roles involve reducing waste in machine learning, but one optimizes training and the other optimizes inference and retrieval.

Perplexity's architecture requires integration across compute allocation, model serving, and real-time search indexing. The shift from his earlier research suggests that once core RL techniques mature, the constraint moves upstream: from algorithmic efficiency to infrastructure that can execute those algorithms reliably at user-facing scale. This is less about inventing new methods and more about orchestrating existing ones through fast, power-hungry systems.

The data does not cover the compute resources Perplexity requires, the power consumption of its infrastructure, or how frequently it refreshes indexed web content. It also does not explain why search-grounded answers require different technical decisions than pure language model inference, though the real-time requirement is noted.
